title: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked: Budgeted Verification Failures in Inherited Agent Memory

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure has not yet passed grounded VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified bilingual deep note carries the mechanism, controls, and lifecycle caveats meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: At a fixed two-record verification budget, stale inherited constraints persist mainly because agents spend verification elsewhere: reallocating one existing slot to the critical provenance path raises current-record-consistent decisions by 61.3–74.0 points across preregistered/replicated settings without helping when the memory is still valid.
analysis.problem: Persistent memories can retain historically correct provenance while becoming behaviorally stale after a newer authoritative record supersedes their content; under a scarce audit budget, provenance availability does not guarantee that the agent will inspect the path that can invalidate a decision-relevant constraint.
analysis.core_idea: Hold the memory form, world state, and two-record verification budget fixed, then randomize only which record one verification slot reaches: native agent allocation, experimenter-forced critical provenance, or a noncritical record. This isolates verification allocation from reasoning and added compute.

memory_design.write: A one-line inherited belief is consolidated from source record S0 at t0; in superseded worlds a later authoritative S1 withdraws the constraint while the stored belief itself is intentionally not reconsolidated.
memory_design.organize: Historical provenance M→S0 stays immutable, while the archive separately records supersession S0→S1 and current-record status; freshness is therefore a relation between memory content and the current authoritative record, not a rewrite of provenance.
memory_design.read: At decision time the agent chooses at most two memory provenance paths to inspect. A single request on the critical path returns S0, its current/superseded status, and S1 when present.
memory_design.update_forget: The experiment diagnoses a missing freshness/supersession verification policy rather than proposing a deployable reconsolidation or forgetting mechanism; the memory remains stale unless the consumer spends budget on its provenance path.

compared_to: Native agent allocation under the same k=2 verification budget
Forced-critical allocation that replaces one native slot with the target provenance path while holding budget fixed
Valid-world controls where the source record agrees with the inherited memory
analysis.evidence: With a stated constraint, native agents inspect its provenance path in 20.1% of primary and 23.1% of fresh-wording episodes. In superseded worlds native decisions follow the stale memory in 77.3%, 74.7%, and 74.7% across primary, replication, and held-out domains. Forced-critical allocation changes current-record-consistent decisions from 34/150→145/150 (+74.0pp), 38/150→147/150 (+72.7pp), and 38/150→130/150 (+61.3pp); a corrected held-out robustness run gives 36/150→146/150 (+73.3pp). When the record still agrees with memory, the same intervention changes outcomes by only 0–2.0pp.
analysis.why_it_matters: This cleanly separates freshness verification from retrieval relevance: a memory can be highly decision-relevant and provenance-rich yet remain harmful if the consumer does not allocate scarce verification to the belief most costly to leave unchecked. The result is a causal allocation diagnosis, not another memory architecture leaderboard.
limitations: The forced-critical arm uses experimenter knowledge of the critical path and is an identification instrument, not a deployable verification scheduler.
The archive makes supersession discoverable in one request; real stores may require multi-hop search, authority resolution, or provenance reconstruction.
The study does not measure how often stale stated constraints occur in deployed memory stores or why native policies under-verify them.
Full storage, index-maintenance, write/reconsolidation, dollar, and energy costs of maintaining freshness metadata are outside the experiment.
